common_name: Little Cuties Frost Heuchera (Miniature Silver Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Little Cuties Frost is a Terra Nova miniature heuchera bred for its icy silver foliage and diminutive scale in containers and small garden pockets.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Little Cuties Frost is a diminutive coral bells cultivar in the Terra Nova Little Cuties series, forming a tight silvery mound with deep burgundy leaf veins and red-tinted undersides that hold their icy sheen from spring through fall. Its dwarf scale and multiple crowns make it well suited to rock garden pockets, trough plantings, and the front edge of a shaded border where a standard-sized heuchera would crowd out neighbors. Slender stems carry pale pink bell flowers well above the foliage from late spring into fall, drawing bees and small pollinators over a long season. Keep soil evenly moist and sharply drained, and divide congested crowns every two to three years in spring to keep the mound tight and vigorous.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries — Heuchera Little Cuties Series
North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

common_name: Little Cuties Sugar Berry Heuchera (Miniature Frosted Purple Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Little Cuties Sugar Berry is a Terra Nova miniature heuchera with frosted purple-pink foliage and a compact habit suited to small containers and tight garden spaces.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Little Cuties Sugar Berry is a compact Terra Nova introduction with crinkled, lobed leaves in frosted silver-purple overlaid with dark gray veining and a lingering blush of pink that persists through most of the growing season. Its small, dense habit suits container plantings, rock gardens, and tight edging where its jewel-toned foliage can be viewed up close. Wiry stems lift small pale flowers just above the leaves from late spring into summer, adding a light, airy accent without overwhelming the tiny mound. Provide consistent moisture and good drainage, and divide clumps every two to three years in spring once the crown becomes congested.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries — Heuchera Little Cuties Series

common_name: Cajun Fire Heuchera (Seasonal Color-Change Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container-grown perennials in spring or fall in fertile, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Cajun Fire is a Terra Nova introduction whose foliage shifts from red to black to maroon across the seasons.

directions: Plant in fertile, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to morning sun, providing consistent moisture if grown with more sun exposure; Cajun Fire is a Terra Nova coral bells selection prized for foliage that shifts through the seasons, opening fiery red in spring, deepening to near-black through summer, then settling into a rich maroon for fall and winter. Its dense, rounded mound of lobed leaves holds its dramatic color better than many older dark-leaved heucheras, making it a strong anchor plant among chartreuse or silver companions in a mixed shade border. Slender dark stems carry airy sprays of small white bell flowers well above the foliage from late spring into summer, attracting bees and hummingbirds. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring and remove tattered winter foliage to keep the crown healthy.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

common_name: Ginger Peach Heuchera (Warm Amber Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container-grown perennials in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Ginger Peach is a Terra Nova introduction bred from 'Ginger Ale' with ruffled peach-to-amber foliage and a vigorous, spreading mound.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with a bit of morning sun to bring out the richest color; Ginger Peach is a vigorous Terra Nova coral bells selection with ruffled leaves that emerge soft peach with a light silvery veil in spring before deepening to a warm ginger-amber tone through summer and winter. Its medium-large, spreading mound fills space quickly, making it a good choice for a shaded foundation planting or a mass grouping where a bold swath of warm foliage color is wanted. Slender stems lift small white flowers well above the leaves in late spring to early summer, drawing bees and other pollinators. Provide even moisture and sharp drainage, and divide crowded clumps every three to four years in spring to renew vigor.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens
